interest: Traces Japan's prewar economic nationalism through foreign corporate buyouts, labor party developments, and wartime dividend restrictions.
keywords: Victor Talking Machine Company of Japan
overview: This file documents Japanese internal economic affairs, corporate regulations, labor movements, and taxation from 1930 to 1939. Key records include diplomatic despatches analyzing pre-election proletarian political parties and the 1931 Labor Union Bill, as well as the buyout of major American and foreign equity holdings in Nipponophone, Yokohama Rubber, and the Victor Talking Machine Company of Japan by domestic conglomerates like Nissan. Additionally, it contains corporate and diplomatic correspondence concerning wartime dividend caps under Article 11 of the National Mobilization Law and the assessment of Japan's Business Profits Tax on American commercial purchasing operations such as Butler Brothers.
